headline: 9 killed in Gaza strikes: Al Jazeera journalist killed, brother died in April
summary: Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least nine people, including a child and a cameraman, in several Gaza locations on Saturday.
details: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least nine people in the Gaza Strip on Saturday, according to health officials. The victims included a child and an Al Jazeera cameraman.
In Gaza City, an airstrike on an apartment building in the Sabra neighborhood killed four Palestinians, including two women and a child. The Israeli military stated it targeted a militant.
Further north in Beit Lahiya, Israeli forces shot and killed a woman, while an airstrike in Khan Younis killed at least one person and wounded eight others.

In the Bureij refugee camp, an airstrike killed three people, including Ahmed Wishah, a cameraman for Al Jazeera. He was killed approximately two months after his brother, Mohammed Wishah, also an Al Jazeera journalist, was killed by Israeli forces.
The Palestinian Journalist Syndicate condemned the killing and noted that nearly 300 Palestinian journalists have been killed since the war began in October 2023.
The Israeli military claimed Ahmed Wishah was a Hamas militant and a sniper, though Al Jazeera and Hamas denied any such affiliation.
Gaza's health ministry reports that over 1,010 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since an October ceasefire, while militants have killed four Israeli soldiers in the same period.
Diplomatic efforts led by the US, Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey to implement a peace plan involving Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawal remain deadlocked.
caption:
An Al Jazeera cameraman was killed in Gaza on Saturday, just two months after his brother, also a journalist, was killed.

Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least nine people in the Gaza Strip on Saturday, according to health officials. The victims included a child and an Al Jazeera cameraman.

In Gaza City, an airstrike on an apartment building in the Sabra neighborhood killed four Palestinians, including two women and a child. The Israeli military stated it targeted a militant.

Further north in Beit Lahiya, Israeli forces shot and killed a woman, while an airstrike in Khan Younis killed at least one person and wounded eight others.

In the Bureij refugee camp, an airstrike killed three people, including Ahmed Wishah, a cameraman for Al Jazeera. He was killed approximately two months after his brother, Mohammed Wishah, also an Al Jazeera journalist, was killed by Israeli forces.

The Palestinian Journalist Syndicate condemned the killing and noted that nearly 300 Palestinian journalists have been killed since the war began in October 2023.

The Israeli military claimed Ahmed Wishah was a Hamas militant and a sniper, though Al Jazeera and Hamas denied any such affiliation.

Gaza's health ministry reports that over 1,010 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since an October ceasefire, while militants have killed four Israeli soldiers in the same period.

Diplomatic efforts led by the US, Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey to implement a peace plan involving Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawal remain deadlocked.

headline_marked: Tax reform: [[Bangladesh proposes year-round return filing]] with 5% early rebate
headline: Tax reform: Bangladesh proposes year-round return filing with 5% early rebate
summary: The 2026-27 budget proposal aims to encourage early submissions by offering a rebate for the first quarter, while introducing penalties for late filers.
details: Bangladesh has proposed allowing individual taxpayers to submit their income tax returns throughout the entire fiscal year, as outlined in the 2026-27 budget proposal.
Under the proposed changes, those filing returns between July 1 and September 30 will be eligible for a 5 percent rebate for early submission, capped at Tk 25,000.

Taxpayers filing in the second quarter (Oct 1 to Dec 31) will face no rebate and no penalties, while those filing in the third quarter (Jan 1 to Mar 31) will face a 2 percent penalty or a maximum of Tk 3,000.
Returns filed in the final quarter (Apr 1 to Jun 30) will attract a 5 percent penalty of tax or a maximum of Tk 5,000.
The proposal comes after repeated extensions of filing deadlines failed to bring in the expected number of taxpayers, prompting revisions through the Finance Bill 2026.
Tax analysts have raised concerns over the lack of detailed mechanisms for the rebate, suggesting that incentives should be adjusted at the point of payment to avoid refund delays.
Currently, taxpayers generally submit returns by November 30, but frequent government extensions have often pushed deadlines into February or March.
caption:

Bangladesh has proposed allowing individual taxpayers to submit their income tax returns throughout the entire fiscal year, as outlined in the 2026-27 budget proposal.

Under the proposed changes, those filing returns between July 1 and September 30 will be eligible for a 5 percent rebate for early submission, capped at Tk 25,000.

Taxpayers filing in the second quarter (Oct 1 to Dec 31) will face no rebate and no penalties, while those filing in the third quarter (Jan 1 to Mar 31) will face a 2 percent penalty or a maximum of Tk 3,000.

Returns filed in the final quarter (Apr 1 to Jun 30) will attract a 5 percent penalty of tax or a maximum of Tk 5,000.

The proposal comes after repeated extensions of filing deadlines failed to bring in the expected number of taxpayers, prompting revisions through the Finance Bill 2026.

Tax analysts have raised concerns over the lack of detailed mechanisms for the rebate, suggesting that incentives should be adjusted at the point of payment to avoid refund delays.

Currently, taxpayers generally submit returns by November 30, but frequent government extensions have often pushed deadlines into February or March.
